News.title: Girl, 10, finds ultra rare creature found in Mexico hidden under Welsh bridge as mum says ‘I thought they were made up’
News.content:
SURPRISE FIND Girl, 10, finds ultra rare creature found in Mexico hidden under Welsh bridge as mum says ‘I thought they were made up’

A TEN-year-old girl was left in awe when she discovered an exceptionally rare Mexican axolotl, the first ever find of its kind in the UK.

Mum Melanie said she was in “shock, disbelief and surprise” when her daughter found the amphibian lurking beneath a bridge in the River Ogmore, Bridgend.





She said Evie was “always finding things” like bugs and newts – but this latest discovery trumped the rest.

No axolotl has been found in the wild in the UK to date – and globally they remain phenomenally rare, with only 50 to 1000 still in existence.

The family, who had been touring Wales in a camper van at the time, saw people talking about this well-known beauty spot online and decided to follow the scent.

Evie was playing in the water under the “Dipping Bridge” at the entrance to Merthyr Mawr village when she lifted up a discarded mat and spotted the axolotl.

The creature appeared to have damage to its tail and stomach.

“I went down to the bank and there was this axolotl there,” said Evie. “I caught it and brought it back.

“I knew what it was straight away because I saw its gills.

“I have seen them on Youtube on Minecraft videos and other videos showing how to look after them.”



Indeed, popularity for the exotic pet has surged in recent years after featuring in games like Minecraft and Roblox.

Evie said her Mum told her not to pick it up, but too excited to let it slip away, she jumped back in the stream and scooped it up with her “bare hands”.

“I went back to my mum and said ‘I’m sorry I broke the rules but look I’ve caught the axolotl,” she said.



“She was quite shocked. We put it in a gravy jug before going to the Range to buy a tub.”

The family decided to cut their holiday short and take the axolotl back home.

After hours of research on how to care for it, the family decided to cut their holiday short so they could take the axolotl back home.

Evie’s named her new pet Dippy D – after the bridge where it was found, and D for the Welsh Dragon. It has been thriving ever since.

“We’ve got a much bigger tank, and we plan to get that set up so it can be transferred,” said Melanie.



The axolotl is a critically endangered species, originating from Lake Xochimilco near Mexico City.

It can grow to 12 inches (30cm) in length but averages around 9 inches (23cm), according to experts.

Chris Newman, director of the National Centre for Reptile Welfare, suggested that the former owner likely released it due to a “change in circumstances”.

He added that it was an illegal practice and “not good from a welfare point of view” but commended Evie for the rescue.

“This is a quite a unique situation, and I think the young female has a keen eye to actually spot it,” he said.



“I think she did remarkably to find him.

“Catching them is no mean feat – they’re quite slippery, so I think she did really well.”

He advised careful consideration when purchasing these amphibious pets, and said they can be “very challenging” to look after given their complex needs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Melanie said her daughter was over the moon with the find. “Evie is delighted with her new pet, they are such amazing creatures.”

“My friends at school think it’s really cool,” said Evie.

News.title: Millionaire big-game hunter, 75, is trampled to death by herd of FIVE elephants while stalking for antelope with shotgun
News.content:
NELLY'S REVENGE Millionaire big-game hunter, 75, is trampled to death by herd of FIVE elephants while stalking for antelope with shotgun

A MILLIONAIRE big-game hunter was trampled to death by a herd of five enraged elephants deep in the African jungle.

Armed with a shotgun and tracking a rare species of antelope, Ernie Dosio, 75, was killed after stumbling across the animals in dense vegetation in Gabon.





The carcass collector had been moving through thick undergrowth with a professional hunter when the pair unknowingly walked into the herd.

The startled beasts charged at the pair without warning.

Dosio was horrifically trampled under the weight of the herd as his companion was hurled to the side.

The animals were said to be so well hidden that it was like they appeared “as if from nowhere”.

A retired game hunter who knew Dosio said: “Whilst in the forest Ernie and his PH (professional hunter) surprised five forest elephant cows with young and feeling under threat the elephants immediately attacked them.

“The professional hunter was attacked first and seriously injured losing his rifle which was knocked from him and lost in the undergrowth leaving Ernie with his shotgun.

“I would rather not go into details but it is safe to assume it would have been quick.”



Safari company Collect Africa confirmed their client died on April 18 after encountering the herd in central Gabon.

Dosio’s body is now being repatriated to his home in California by the US embassy in Gabon.

Gabon is home to around 60 per cent of the world’s remaining forest elephants, with roughly 50,000 living deep within its dense forests.

African elephants are the largest land animals on Earth, weighing up to four tonnes and reaching speeds of up to 25mph.

At the time of his death, Dosio was hunting a rare species of antelope and hoped to add the yellow-backed duiker to his extensive trophy collection.



Tributes have since poured in for the father-of-two.

Lodi Lodge secretary Tommy Whitman said in a statement: “It is with a most heavy heart and sadness that I am reporting the passing of Ernie Dosio.

“May all of our thoughts and prayers go out to his family and loved ones.

“Ernie always had his hand in his pocket and would help out those who needed it be it war veterans or handicapped or underprivileged kids.

“He would never want recognition but he was always there with a loving heart.



“He will be really missed around here and was one of the real good guys.”

A family friend said: “Ernie with his big moustache was larger than life but did not show it off.

“He was just a farmer and good old country boy who loved to hunt and fish. There’s not many in the US today who would have a trophy collection to match Ernie’s.

“The news of his death in Africa was like a bomb going off.”

Over the decades, Dosio had hunted some of the world’s most dangerous animals, including elephants, lions and buffalo.



Back home, he was also known for pursuing nearly every species of wild deer as part of his collection.

This is not the first time a millionaire big game hunter has been killed.

In August last year, Asher Watkins was brutally gored to death by a buffalo he was stalking with a guide in South Africa.

The Cape Buffalo – known to hunters as Black Death – charged him from a blind spot, impaling him on one of its horns.

The professional hunter with him desperately fought to save him but the area they were in was so remote he bled to death before help could arrive.



“He was beyond help except to load his body into the ambulance. He had horrific injuries to his stomach and to his ribs,” paramedics said.

“He was beyond help except to load his body into the ambulance. He had horrific injuries to his stomach and to his ribs.

“It was big buffalo and anything standing in the way of a charge would not survive. If left alone they are pretty tolerant but if you upset them it will not end well.

Watkins was also a conversationalist who believed hunting was a vital part of the preserving wildlife.

In July last year, there was worldwide anger when a much-loved lion called Blondie was lured way from its reserve and shot dead by a trophy hunter.



Delvy Workman, 48, was named and shamed as the man who pulled the trigger in Zimbabwe.

News.title: Putin unleashes snarling propagandists on Harry after prince demanded Kremlin dictator end Ukraine war on Kyiv visit
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin unleashed an army of propagandists on the Royal Family after Prince Harry urged the tyrant to end his Ukraine war.

The Duke of Sussex made an unannounced visit to Kyiv on Thursday – only a week after a massive Russian aerial attack – to address world leaders and military top brass at the Kyiv Security Forum.





Directly appealing to the Russian President, he warned that “no country benefits from the continued loss of life we are witnessing” – provoking a furious response from Moscow.

“This is the prince who was photographed in a Nazi uniform, right?” the Russia-1 anchor, Vladimir Solovyov, asked.

Solovyov routinely slurs the Ukrainian government as being Nazi, echoing Putin who has frequently cited the need to “denazify” the country as the primary justification for the full-scale invasion.



“This Harry…came to join his Nazi brothers [in Ukraine],” he told his viewers.

Following up with a sickening racial smear about Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, he then addressed Harry: “You came here to act like a clown….

“What does this have to do with you?

“Was that your relative [Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor] hanging out on Epstein Island…? Who are you?



“Who gave you the right to even discuss these matters? You don’t deserve any respect. You came with your Nazi buddies, why didn’t you wear the right uniform?”

By convention, the Royal Family do not speak out on any political matters – but King Charles and other senior royals have previously voiced their support for Ukraine.

For Harry, this is his third visit ⁠to the country since the war ​began, ⁠used far more explicit language than any of his relatives have done in the past.

“President Putin, no nation benefits from the continued loss of life we are witnessing,” he said in a speech to a Kyiv security forum.

“There is still a moment – now – to stop this war, to ​stop ⁠further suffering for Ukrainians and Russians ‌alike, and to choose a different course.”



He also called on the US to do more to bring about an end to the invasion, provoking a strong response from Donald Trump himself.

“This is a ‌moment for American leadership, a moment for America to show that it can honour its international treaty obligations,” the prince said.

“Europe has stood up in profound ways,

“The task now is to match endurance with speed, solidarity with scale, and commitment with consistency.”

Responding to the criticism, the US President hit back: “I am speaking for the UK more than Prince Harry, that’s for sure. But thank him for his advice.”



During Harry’s visit to Kyiv, Russian sprawling attacks on Ukraine killed at least six people and injured another 40.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Russia unleashed two Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 107 drones, the Air Force said, adding that 96 were intercepted.

Strikes continued this morning, with drones targeting the Ukrainian capital. So far, no injuries have been reported.

News.title: Stalker, 38, who sewed pigeon heads onto dolls & told female BrewDog worker ‘I love you’ in graffiti is found dead
News.content:
DARK OBSESSION Stalker, 38, who sewed pigeon heads onto dolls & told female BrewDog worker ‘I love you’ in graffiti is found dead

A DANGEROUS stalker who sewed pigeon heads onto dolls and told a bar worker “I love you” in graffiti died in his flat after being freed from jail.

Daniel William Fairbairn, 38, left a young female BrewDog employee “shaking with fear” after he became obsessed with her.





While searching the twisted stalker’s home after he was arrested, cops discovered dolls with pigeon heads sewn onto them.

The gruesome find caused a stir among police and mental health staff with Fairbairn explaining away the horrifying items by saying he was “practising taxidermy.”

Norfolk Coroner’s Court later heard John Keane, of the custody liaison and diversion team, did not accept Fairbairn’s bizarre explanation.

He said: “Due to this information and my past clinical experience it indicated to me that he was practising fantasy-based scenarios.



“Taxidermy did not make sense.”

While in custody, Fairbairn claimed to live an alternative lifestyle, saying he used his kitchen as a workshop, collected items from bins and painted the walls of his home black.

Because his lifestyle could “cause issues”, Fairbairn said he dressed like a cowboy to avoid people.

Officers raided his home when he was convicted of stalking a female worker at BrewDog Norwich.



Fairbairn pleaded guilty to charges of stalking, possession of a knife in a public place and criminal damage.

He became obsessed with the woman and would pursue her relentlessly, causing her fear and distress, a court heard.

He was arrested after an incident that saw him loiter outside the city centre pub with a knife.

After his release from custody, Fairbairn was found dead in his home in Mousehold, Norwich, in September last year when concerns were raised about a smell coming from the property.

During his time in custody, the twisted stalker was assessed by registered mental health nurse Steven Webster.



It was said that Fairbairn failed to understand the seriousness of the allegations against him.

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

He also allegedly gave an unbelievable account of the events that led to his arrest.

Fairbairn, who had recently experienced homelessness, said he would be “disappointed” if he was locked up.

A previous psychiatric admission, history of self-harm and mental health difficulties were flagged by mental health professionals when Fairbairn was jailed.

The stalker is understood to have been suffering from PTSD after witnessing his friend take his own life.



He is also said to have been battling depression, anxiety and self-harm.

Fairbairn would report PTSD, depression and anxiety to a doctor who saw him in custody in 2025, but he was not expressing suicidal thoughts at the time.

But, mental health staff would conclude that he was not psychotic and he was discharged from mental health input while behind bars.

In August 2025, he was given a suspended sentence which included 12 months of mental health treatment requirement.

He was also banned from entering the city centre but during an appointment on August 18 he appeared confused about the requirements.



Fairbairn, who said he had no support network, was given a food bank voucher and said he wanted to make a fresh start, the inquest heard.

The stalker claimed he enjoyed going to the gym and riding his bike but admitted he found socialising “difficult unless trust had been built first”.

Fairbairn would engage well at another meeting before staff lost contact with him.

Several messages were sent to his phone but there was no reply.

Giving evidence to the coroner’s court, his sister Nicole said: “He didn’t have friends as he was quiet and scared to make friends because when he did he lost them. This made his mental health worse.



“He told us not to believe everything in the press. They tarred his name and embarrassed him.

“He felt like he didn’t have a way out, he was talking about leaving his flat and living in the woods.”

According to Nicole, it wasn’t unusual not to hear from her brother for months at a time; she added that he would have been deeply hurt by his ban from the city centre.

Fairbairn’s body was found on September 3 after a gas engineer raised concerns over a smell coming from the stalker’s flat.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There was no note and no suspicious circumstances were identified, the coroner heard.



Area coroner Johanna Thompson recorded a conclusion of suicide.

News.title: Chilling moment ex-beauty queen is shot dead by jealous mother-in-law – whose son then gives shockingly callous reaction
News.content:
THIS is the chilling moment a former beauty queen is shot dead by her mother-in-law in front of her months-old baby.

New mum Carolina Flores Gomez, 27, was fatally shot 12 times in her head, neck and face in a luxury apartment in Mexico City.





Her mother-in-law Erika Herrera, 63, was seen holding the gun just seconds before the shots rang out.

In spine-chilling footage, Carolina’s husband Alejandro Gomez had a callous, nonchalant reaction when he realised the mother of his child had been fatally shot.

Just seconds after the new mum was hunted down and killed in her own living room, Gomez was seen walking into the frame of the video carrying their eight-month-old baby.



“What was that?” he asked his mother in Spanish.

“What did you do, crazy?” an unidentified woman’s voice is heard saying.

“Nothing,” Herrera, 63, answered. She made me angry.”

“What’s wrong with you? She’s my family,” Gomez said, calmly.



Herrera answered “you’re mine and she stole you”.

Carolina had been seen walking through the living room wearing a white-patterned robe.

She had her back to Herrera, unaware of the violent attack about to unfold.

Just seconds after Carolina entered a room out of view of the camera, a shot rang out, followed by her screaming.

Several further shots echoed through the flat before there was a moment of silence.



Tragically, a playpen, a stroller and children’s toys could all be seen in the video inside the luxury apartment in Polanco, Mexico City.

The family did not report the April 15 shooting to the police until the following day.

Mexico City cops have since launched an investigation.



While officers have not yet pressed charges, they identified Herrera as the prime suspect.

They said they are making inquiries as to why the family delayed reporting the fatal ordeal.

Carolina’s mum – Reyna Gomez Molina – told Univision News that Gomez had not immediately reported the shooting over concern for the couple’s young baby.

She said her son-in-law had worried that the child would end up in a foster home.



Carolina made a name for herself when she won Miss Teen Universe for Baja California in 2017.

She went on to represent the state in the national beauty pageant.

The crowned beauty queen moved to the capital after leaving the port city of Ensenada on Mexico’s Baja California peninsula.

Carolina’s friend Alexa Villalobos posted an emotional tribute to social media, saying: “Carolina was beautiful inside and out; loving, charismatic, and helpful”.

“It seems impossible to believe that someone with so much grace could leave in this way; the snatching away of a life full of dreams and love is something unforgivable,” she wrote.



“I want justice for Caro, for her family, her mother, her little sister, and her baby, who were her greatest happiness.”

Carolina’s mum organised a protest march over the weekend, demanding justice for her daughter.

“Let’s raise our voices for my daughter so that her name is not just another statistic,” she wrote on social media.



Friends and family continued to post their own tributes online for the young mum.

Her old school El Tesoro del Saber posted touching photos of her throughout the years, saying: “With deep sadness we want to express our most sincere condolences for the irreparable loss of our former student Carolina Flores Gomez, who was part of our community from her earliest years.”

“Although time has passed, we fondly remember her time at our school and the joy she shared with us.

“We join in the grief of her family and loved ones, sending them a hug full of solidarity. Rest in peace.”

“Your teachers will always remember you as that beautiful little girl, full of love and tenderness,” the post added.



Herrera’s whereabouts are unknown.

Mexico City prosecutors revealed they were investigating the incident under the country’s “femicide protocol”.

“Ministerial, forensic, and field investigation procedures have been carried out continuously, including the involvement of specialized personnel at the scene, the processing of evidence, and actions to identify the person indicated as the probable responsible party,” they said.

“Likewise, comprehensive support is being provided to the victim’s family members.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The investigation remains ongoing.

News.title: Temperatures set to hit 21C today before balmy weekend with thousands flocking to beaches & parks
News.content:
SUN'S OUT Temperatures set to hit 21C today before balmy weekend with thousands flocking to beaches & parks

BRITS are set for a balmy weekend with thousands flocking to beaches and parks as temperatures are expected to climb up to 21C today.

This weekend is set to be hotter than Ibiza with the return of warmer weather and clear skies.





Across the south of England and Wales, today’s temps are expected to soar up to a glorious 21C, according to the Met Office.

Other parts of the UK such as Cambridge, Stoke-on-Trent and Leeds could see highs of 19C this afternoon, as seen on the Met Office’s weather map.

For many, today will see blue skies and sunshine with moderate UV levels, said the forecaster.

The warm weather will continue into the weekend with cities including Manchester, London and Birmingham expected to at least see 21C tomorrow.

In contrast, Ibiza is set to reach highs of 18C over the weekend, according to the Met Office.

Steven Keates, Deputy Chief Forecaster said: “High pressure will remain broadly in charge of the UK’s weather for the remainder of this week and into the weekend.

“Most places will remain dry with a fair amount of sunshine too.

“As is often the case, there are a few exceptions, with cloudier conditions for some at times and patchy rain possible for northern Scotland later in the weekend, so keep an eye on the forecast as the week progresses



“In the sunshine, we’re expecting temperatures to steadily climb, likely peaking in the low twenties on Friday and over the weekend.

“Onshore breezes will keep some coastal areas somewhat cooler.

“And gardeners beware, where skies are clear and winds light overnight, a patchy frost is also likely.”

Eddy Leviten, Executive Director at Tourism Alliance said: “This is when the UK shows what it does best.

“Few destinations can match the range on offer, with coast, countryside, heritage, events, attractions, culture, and cities, all within easy reach.



“For our members, it’s a clear window to drive bookings, support jobs and deliver real value to the UK economy. The visitor economy is one of our biggest economic sectors, worth £147bn.”

After days of bright sunshine and above-average temperatures boosted growth, the UK is set to see home-grown strawberries arriving on supermarket shelves today.

Punnets will begin to arrive on Tesco shelves in Surrey, Kent, Herefordshire and some London stores from Friday, with nearly half the country to follow on next week, the supermarket said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The grocer expects to receive 300 tonnes of UK-grown fruit next week – roughly one million punnets – up by more than 100% just three weeks ago.

The whole of the UK is set to be supplied by mid-May, meaning retailers will have to rely less on Spanish and Moroccan imports in the next few weeks.

News.title: Teen ‘told 999 handler she was being blackmailed by predator but was sexually assaulted after being advised to meet him’
News.content:
GRIM MISTAKE Teen ‘told 999 handler she was being blackmailed by predator but was sexually assaulted after being advised to meet him’

A MET 999 call handler told a teen girl to meet up with a blackmailing predator who then sexually assaulted her, a tribunal heard.

Jennifer Gordon received a call from the “the upset and scared” 17-year-old who told her a man had sexually assaulted her sister and was blackmailing her by threatening to release indecent pictures.



Instead of telling her not to meet the man under any circumstances, she suggested the teen could see him in a public place to reduce risk.



Following the call, the girl met up with the fiend and was allegedly sexually assaulted.

Gordon was sacked by the Met Police but took the case to an employment tribunal, claiming she had been the victim of race and disability discrimination.

She has now lost her case – with the tribunal finding she had not shown remorse.

Gordon was employed as a Communications Officer by the Met between July 2002 and August 2023.

The role involved handling between 60 and 80 999 and 101 calls everyday.

She was previously dismissed for gross misconduct in 2016 but that penalty was reduced to a written warning and she underwent further training.

On August 4, 2021, she answered a 999 call from the girl, who reported a recent sexual assault on her 16-year-old sister by a 20-year-old man after he plied her with alcohol.

She sounded “young, upset and scared’ during the phone call and started crying”, it was said.



The man had threatened to share “explicit sexual images” unless she met up with him.

She feared police coming to her home but Gordon told her she could not report the threats to officers unless she was accompanied by an adult, which was “incorrect” advice.

The tribunal heard “at no point did Gordon advise the caller not to meet the perpetrator”.

She instead advised her that if she was to go see him to delete the pictures, she should “meet him in a public place to minimise the risk”.

The tribunal heard: “On any commonsense view, that advice was inappropriate and put the caller at risk.”



In a transcript of the call, Gordon said: “If you’re under 18 you wouldn’t be able to go by yourself but if you’ve got someone like an aunt or a cousin or someone like that , that is over 18 , they could go with you to report it if you don’t want us coming to your home.”

The girl then asked: “So you think I should go and then just delete it?’

Gordon replied: “Watch him delete it, if he doesn’t delete it then you know, you know, that he can’t be trusted but he probably can’t be trusted anyway … because he’s using that to get you where, get you to the location, but if you do end up going, don’t go alone.

“Maybe go with a group, a group of friends and also don’t go to his home or any place, go to a place where there’s CCTV cameras like some sort of restaurant or something like that, you know, some sort of food courts or something like that but don’t go along and don’t to a quiet place where he can get you off by himself and then watch and see if he deletes it.

“If he doesn’t delete it after you meet him then you know that you can’t trust him anyway but I’m not saying you should, it depends on what threats he’s made.”



Following the call, Gordon failed to record a crime code and wrongly graded it.

This meant no offences were recorded on the system and the call was not passed on or brought to the attention of a supervisor.

Gordon later admitted she might have “forgotten” to pass it on to her supervisor.

She also conceded that since the caller had made two criminal allegations, then she should have put in a criminal offence code.

A gross misconduct hearing took place in August 2023 and the panel confirmed that Gordon had provided incorrect advice, misclassification and no safeguarding.



She took claims of unfair dismissal, disability discrimination, unfavourable treatment, failure to make reasonable adjustments, disability harassment, victimisation, race discrimination and race harassment to a tribunal.

Gordon claimed she had been the victim of disability discrimination because she was made to continue working when she thought she had been suspended.

She said that her suspension gave the Met Police the chance “to take potshots at her”.

But all her claims were dismissed by the employment tribunal, who found the Met had undertaken a “fair” process and were worried it could happen again.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Employment Judge Sarah Matthews said: “It would be clear to a reasonable person listening to the call, even without any training or experience, that a potential crime could well occur and that the report needed to be followed up urgently.



“[Ms Gordon] should have advised the caller not to meet the perpetrator under any circumstances.”

News.title: Dramatic moment Ukrainian officer hacks presentation to Russian would-be recruits – & warns: ‘I’ll have to kill you all’
News.content:
THIS is the astonishing moment a Ukrainian soldier successfully infiltrates a Russian university to warn students they face certain death if they go to war.

The masked man appears via video link, posing as a Russian fighter to conceal his true identity.





University bosses invited who they thought was one of their countrymen to speak at a recruitment drive for Vladimir Putin‘s war machine.

These sessions pressure impressionable students into signing army contracts.

They are held regularly across the country to bolster numbers for Putin’s forces, which are reportedly losing up to 30,000 soldiers a month.



After being given the floor, the trickster reveals his true identity to stunned students at Kuban State University in Krasnodar.

“I am, in fact, a soldier, just not Russian, but Ukrainian,” he says.

“And I want to tell you, God forbid you go there.

“I will have to kill you, every one of you who signs this contract.”



As things spiral out of control, university professors scramble to cut the feed.

However, they are unable to do so before he issues a final chilling warning to the captivated audience.

“Your faces are all sketched out,” he says.

“The frontline hasn’t moved for four years now, and it’s standing still.

“And, honestly, every one who comes onto Ukrainian soil, we will kill every one of them.”



The professors finally cut the link as the screens in the lecture hall go blank.

This comes as approval ratings for Vladimir Putin’s premiership have drastically dropped in Russia.

In a huge warning sign for the Kremlin leader, only 71 per cent of Russians continue to support their president, according to state-affiliated polling institute FOM.

A drop of five per cent marked the steepest decline in popularity ratings for the dictator since 2019, analysts say.

Much of this decline relates to the war in Ukraine – something which Russians are forbidden to complain about.



Talks between Russia and Ukraine have stalled in recent weeks while the US looks to resolve its own conflict in the Middle East.

The last summit where all three parties were present took place in Saudi Arabia back in February.

Ukrainian representatives called for a full withdrawal of Russian troops and restoration of any lost territory.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Moscow signalled openness to negotiations but insisted on recognition of the territories they currently occupy.

No agreement was reached but participants agreed to keep diplomatic channels open for discussion.

News.title: 'Homes look stylish' with 'modern' £15 B&M furniture similar to £42 B&Q version
News.content:
'Homes look stylish' with 'modern' £15 B&M furniture similar to £42 B&Q version

The £15 furniture looks similar to a pricier version at B&Q

View 3 Images B&M shoppers can save less by opting for the £15 lookalike version (Image: Getty )

B&M shoppers can 'style up their homes' with a £15 piece of furniture that could be easily mistaken for a pricier version at another high-street store. As part of B&M's latest collection of homeware, the store is selling a storage unit that it says 'adds style to homes'.

‌



For £15, customers can get the Simply Three Cube Unit in pale oak. The rectangular unit comes with three shelves, allowing shoppers space to store belongings or to decorate with various books, ornaments and more.

‌



In the product description, B&M says: "Style up your home with this modern and practical three Cube Unit. Finished in a soft pale oak, this cube unit is a versatile storage piece that perfectly complements modern spaces."

‌



It adds: "Perfect for books, décor, baskets, and everyday essentials." The unit is 30cm wide, 23cm deep and 80cm tall. You can browse more Storage Furniture online, or buy in-store at B&M.

B&M is also selling a Two Cube version of the same storage unit, with two storage compartments rather than three, for just £10. For anyone after more space, there is a Six Cube option on sale, with six compartments, for £20.

View 3 Images B&M's £15 Simply Three Cube Unit in Pale Oak (Image: B&M)

‌



B&M's £15 Simply Three Cube Unit could be easily mistaken for B&Q's Grey Sonoma Book TV Cabinet, which features three storage compartments and comes in a similar colour. However, the DIY store's version costs more at £42.30.

On B&Q's website, the product description reads: "Featuring a sleek and classic design, this book cabinet makes a decorative as well as practical addition to your decor. Durable material: The engineered wood is of exceptional quality with a smooth surface and also features strength, stability and resistance to moisture.

"Ample storage space: With three compartments, this book shelf can offer ample storage space for keeping your magazines, books, DVDs, multimedia devices and other decorative items well organised and within reach. Multiple functions: This book rack can meet your different requirements for it can be used as a storage rack or display shelf in the living room. Besides, it can be placed horizontally as a TV cabinet as well."

‌



View 3 Images B&Q's £42 Book Cabinet TV Cabinet Grey Sonoma (Image: B&Q)

While the two storage units look similar, there are a few differences, besides price. B&Q's version is slightly bigger, measuring 36cm wide, 30cm deep and 114cm tall. B&Q also claims the unit's "durable" engineered wood construction ensures "strength, stability, and moisture resistance".

Elsewhere at B&M, people could inject a "clean and natural" touch to homes with a living room set that B&M claims to "complement most interiors". Shoppers might want to consider this bundle when updating their spaces, as it's more budget-friendly than other stores' bundles.

Article continues below

Describing the set online, B&M bosses wrote: "Add versatility and modern style to your living room with this Home Collection Set of Two Tables. Featuring a modern panelled style with a clean and natural finish, this pair of tables effortlessly elevates any living space and complements most interiors."

News.title: Millionaire trophy hunter, 75, trampled by five angry elephants during African hunt
News.content:
Millionaire trophy hunter, 75, trampled by five angry elephants during African hunt

Ernie Dosio's home was decorated with mounts of exotic animal heads but was killed in a stampede of angry elephants earlier this month while stalking a rare deer in Africa

View 9 Images Ernie Dosio's home was decorated with mounts of exotic animal heads (Image: bobbyhansensafaris.com)

A millionaire trophy hunter has been killed by a herd of five angry elephants while hunting antelope.

‌



Vineyard owner Ernie Dosio was trampled to death by the stampede as he stalked through a thick forest in central Africa.

‌



The 75-year-old displayed a vast collection of exotic animal heads across trophy rooms in his home in Lodi, 30 miles south of Sacramento, California, including elephant, rhino, bear, buffalo, crocodile, lion, zebra and leopard. Dosio also shot and killed almost every species of buck in the US, including elk, moose and reindeer, which are also mounted to the walls of his private function rooms.

‌



Dosio met his demise on April 17 when the veteran hunter was ambushed by a herd of elephants as he hunted a small forest antelope in the Lope area of Gabon. The hunt was on for a £30,000 shot at the secretive and elusive yellow backed duiker.

View 9 Images The hunter had a huge collection of exotic animal heads (Image: Bobby Hansen Hunting Safaris)

The father-of-two, who had a licence which allowed him to hunt dwarf forest buffalo in Gabon, but was only permitted a shotgun for the deer hunt, stood little chance against the herd of five as they guarded a young calf.

‌



African elephants are the world's largest living land animal, with females standing as high as 12 feet tall and weighing nearly four tons. They can also reach speeds of up to 25mph in a charge.

The elephants were well hidden in the dense undergrowth at the time, and appeared "as if from nowhere".

View 9 Images African elephants can reach speeds of 25mph (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Dosio's shotgun was cast aside as the startled herd turned on him and his professional hunter. While the hunter was left seriously injured and lost his weapon in the thick bush during the attack, Dosio was brutally trampled underfoot and killed.

His body is now in the process of being repatriated by the US Embassy in Gabon to Lodi in California. He is survived by his long-term partner, Betty, and two children.

Dosio was the owner of the Pacific AgriLands Inc which has its own 12,000 acre vineyard in Modesto but specialises in providing management for local wine farms. His son, Jeff, is President of the company which produces 40 percent of Californian wines. His other son, Blake, is a farmer and reportedly also worked in the family business. The company supports most local vineyards, including the famous E&J Gallo wines.

‌



View 9 Images Ernie Dosio has been described as a "really nice guy" in tributes (Image: bobbyhansensafaris.com)

A retired game hunter in Cape Town who knows the victim said: “Ernie has been hunting since he could hold a rifle and has many trophies from Africa and the US.

“Although many disagree with big game hunting all Ernie’s hunts were strictly licensed and above board and were registered as conservation in culling animal numbers.

‌



“Ernie had booked a hunt for dwarf forest buffalo and duikers, in particular the yellow backed duiker, and under strict licensing laws he could not take along his own guns.

“The hunting company would supply a shotgun and cartridges for the duiker hunt.

“Whilst in the forest Ernie and his PH (professional hunter) surprised 5 forest elephant cows with young and feeling under threat the elephants immediately attacked them.

‌



View 9 Images Dosio's trophy room where he kept countless trophies from the decades of his hunts (Image: Supplied to Jamie Pyatt News Ltd)

“The professional hunter was attacked first and seriously injured losing his rifle which was knocked from him and lost in the undergrowth leaving Ernie with his shotgun.

“I would rather not go into detail but it is safe to assume it would have been quick.

‌



“Ernie was a very well-known and popular hunter in the US and in Africa and a very keen conservationist and he did a hell of a lot of charity work and was a really good guy.

View 9 Images The group were guarding a calf (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

“What happened has been deeply felt by many each side of the Atlantic” he said.

‌



Safari company Collect Africa also confirmed the death of a client on April 17 in a brief statement, saying he and the professional hunter had encountered five elephant cows and a calf during a hunt for a yellow backed duiker.

Ernie was a life member of hunting group California Wildfowl and a mainstay in the Sacramento Safari Club. He also help the post of Great Elk in the Californian Central District Elks, a charitable group of patriotic Americans, known for supporting philanthropic programs such as military veterans, youth scholarships and disaster relief.

Lodi Lodge secretary Tommy Whitman said in a Facebook statement yesterday: “It is with a most heavy heart and sadness that I am reporting the passing of Ernio Dosio.

‌



View 9 Images Dosio posing with a lion he shot in Southern Africa in 2016 (Image: bobbyhansensafaris.com)

“May all of our thoughts and prayers go out to his family and loved ones. Ernie was Great Elk for 30 years and a pillar in our community who will be sorely missed”.

He added afterwards: “Ernie always had his hand in his pocket and would help out those who needed it be it war veterans or handicapped or underprivileged kids.

‌



“He would never want recognition but he was always there with a loving heart.

“Ernie’s passion was hunting and he spent much of his time either hunting here in the USA or in Africa and most of his trophies are on display at his own trophy rooms.

“He will be really missed around here and was one of the real good guys” he said.

‌



View 9 Images More of his trophy rooms (Image: Supplied to Jamie Pyatt News Ltd)

A representative of Pacific AgriLand inc added: “Nobody here at present is available to speak. That has to be down to his son Jeff when he is ready to say something to you.

“Ernie was very popular and Jeff is taking many calls as you can well imagine. It is a huge tragedy" she said.

‌



A family friend said: “Ernie would hold a charity function there every month where food was served to members of the Elk lodges and upstanding citizens of the community.

“There would be judges, advocates and the heads of the local vineyards and big noises from industry and commerce and it was where all the local networking was done.

“It was always a huge fundraiser with money raised going to help those who needed it.

‌



View 9 Images A friend has described him as having a 'larger than life' personality (Image: wagonhoundoutfitters.com)

“Ernie with his big moustache was larger than life but did not show it off although he had money he was not one for the big house or fancy cars or the jet-set lifestyle.

“He was a just a farmer and good old country boy who loved to hunt and fish. There are not many in the US today who would have a trophy collection to match Ernie’s.

Article continues below

"The news of his death in Africa was like a bomb going off here. It has been said the elephants came out of nowhere. One thing is for sure he will get a huge send off."

News.title: Jet2 new flight update for passengers worried about upcoming holidays
News.content:
Jet2 new flight update for passengers worried about upcoming holidays

The travel company issued a message for passengers who have booked with Jet2.com and Jet2holidays

View 3 Images Jet2 replies to passengers on social media (Image: Getty)

Jet2 has issued advice for passengers ahead of the summer holidays. Many UK customers have shared concerns about upcoming flights on social media in recent weeks, following reports of possible fuel shortages.

‌



However, Jet2 has said it sees "no reason not to look forward to operating our scheduled programme of flights and holidays as normal." The airline offered reassurance to passengers after a social media user contacted Jet2tweets on X. Jet2.com and Jet2holidays customers regularly raise questions on the travel company's social media page.

‌



In a recent post, a passenger named Darren wrote: "Hello Jet2 we are looking at booking a holiday, what’s the situation with jet fuel, if you delay/cancel will we get a full refund? As opposed to offering vouchers or rescheduling?"

‌



Answering the question, Jet2 replied to the passenger and confirmed its response for the Mirror. Jet2 said: "We remain in continual dialogue with our fuel suppliers, as is standard practice. Based on the conversations we have been having, we see no reason not to look forward to operating our scheduled programme of flights and holidays as normal.

"We understand that our customers work and save very hard for their holidays, and we are looking forward to making sure that they enjoy their award-winning Jet2holidays." Customers can view the latest travel information on Jet2.com.

View 3 Images Passengers are looking forward to the summer holidays (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

‌



The EU has warned that Europe faces a "very serious crisis" over aviation fuel supplies, which could be affected by the war in Iran. "Unfortunately, it's very likely that many people's holidays will be affected, either by flight cancellations or very, very expensive tickets," Dan Jorgensen, the EU energy commissioner, told Sky News. "Even if we do everything we can do, if the jet fuel is not there, then it's not there."

However, Parliamentary Under Secretary for Transport Keir Mather previously said that "there is no immediate cause for concern relating to fuel stocks." Liberal Democrat MP for Eastleigh Liz Jarvis tabled a question for the Secretary of State for Transport.

On April 17, Keir Mather replied: " The Government is monitoring the impact of the conflict in the Middle East on fuel supplies, including jet fuel. In coordination with the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero we have worked with fuel suppliers, airlines and airports to understand levels of jet fuel and pricing.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Jet2 responded to the passenger's message (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

"There is no immediate cause for concern relating to fuel stocks, and speculation will not help airlines or passengers. Many airlines lock in fuel prices in advance, to help protect tickets from spikes in price. We encourage all airlines to do what they can to ensure tickets remain fairly and appropriately priced for passengers."

Tim Jeans, a former commercial director at Ryanair who was later managing director of Monarch Air, has said while there “may be some trimming of schedules” by airlines he did not expect firms to cancel routes altogether. His comments come in the wake of warnings from the trade body for European airports that there could be a “systemic” shortage of jet fuel ahead of the peak summer season if the Strait of Hormuz does not reopen in the weeks ahead.

News.title: 'I found different way to buy house and contracts were signed immediately'
News.content:
'I found different way to buy house and contracts were signed immediately'

A young first-time buyer from London shared how she purchased a Putney property and avoided being gazumped

View 3 Images Sophie Tavener (Image: Sophie Tavener/Propertymark)

The UK's housing market has experienced a significant transformation in recent years, with growing numbers drawn to the straightforward nature of auction purchases, according to an industry body.

‌



Propertymark's latest Auctions Barometer Report reveals that a substantial proportion of auctioneers surveyed (54 per cent) reported an increase in available lots across all property types compared to the previous year.

‌



Propertymark highlighted numerous factors behind the rising popularity of auctions, particularly amongst first-time buyers who are 'chain-free', with the primary appeal being the rapid pace of potential property transactions. The organisation's research indicates that housing transactions currently take more than 17 weeks to complete in a persistently high number of cases.

‌



The auction process, by contrast, can accelerate sales because the purchase contract is formed immediately after bidding concludes, offering both sellers and buyers enhanced reassurance. Additionally, the starting guide price for many properties is typically pitched at a level designed to generate stronger initial interest.

Properties sold through auction frequently employ a varied mix of in-room bidding and online platforms. This was certainly a key factor for first-time buyer Sophie Tavener from London, who chose to purchase a Putney property through an online auction she discovered on an online property portal.

View 3 Images Inside the house (Image: Sophie Tavener/Propertymark)

‌



"I definitely found the properties being auctioned more affordable, though the one I purchased needed a lot of renovation," Sophie explained.

She added: "I had gone down the estate agency route before and I had been gazumped (where a seller accepts a higher offer from a new buyer after previously accepting an offer from someone else) twice. I saw a property that was being sold via auction. I did research into the auctioning route and I thought I would give it a go."

Sophie revealed that social media and online research into the legal paperwork provided to both buyers and sellers throughout the auction process had equipped her with much of the information she needed to get her head around it all.

‌



While Sophie described the auction route as 'daunting' initially, she explained that once she grasped how it functioned, it wasn't vastly different from the conventional estate agent approach, as she still had the opportunity to view the property beforehand and pose questions that were crucial to her decision-making. When the online auction day arrived, Sophie shared her feelings about the experience.

"I found it very exciting. It was a quick process, which can be a little bit exhilarating. The day of the auction itself made me think I was going to be outbid for the property, but I got it," Sophie said.

View 3 Images Inside the house Sophie bought at auction (Image: Sophie Tavener/Propertymark)

Article continues below

Furthermore, as the auctioneer Sophie collaborated with held NAVA Propertymark qualifications, giving them the expertise to navigate the legal complexities of the auction process, she described herself as 'very happy' to work with them, citing the extensive legal documentation they supplied.

She added: "I would recommend it to other first-time buyers because I think you get a fantastic outcome that is ideal for my generation. It is not daunting, as many people make it out to be, because you can state the maximum price you want to pay and you avoid getting gazumped."

Enlisting a qualified auctioneer can significantly improve the auction experience, thanks to their specialist training in understanding the legal obligations involved. Prospective buyers can use Propertymark's Find an Expert tab to locate a qualified auctioneer in their local area.

News.title: Murder suspect named after Stretford headteacher killed in crash while out cycling
News.content:
Murder suspect named after Stretford headteacher killed in crash while out cycling

Police raced to the scene on Monday (April 20) to reports a cyclist, later confirmed as the head of a local school, had been killed in a horrific collision with a car in Altrincham

View 3 Images Michael Mullins was killed in the collision on Monday (Image: Manchester Evening News )

A man has been charged with murder after the tragic death of a headteacher.

Cyclist Michael Mullins was declared dead at the scene of the crash on Monday. Greater Manchester Police has confirmed a man has been charged after the horrific crash on Paddock Lane, in Altrincham, at around 6.10pm on April 20.

Simon Richardson, 34, of no fixed address, has been charged with murder, manslaughter, dangerous driving, failing to stop, and driving without insurance, the force confirmed in a statement this morning (Friday).

He has been remanded in custody and is due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates Court later today, the Manchester Evening News reports.

View 3 Images Tributes have been pouring in for the teacher (Image: Greater Manchester Police/family handout)

Mr Mullins, 56, who lived in Weaverham near Northwich, had been the headteacher of Stretford Grammar School for 17 years. Heartfelt tributes described him as a "loving dad, husband, brother-in-law, 'Diddy', uncle, son-in-law".

In a statement, the family said: "He was devoted to his family and our lives will never be the same. A gap has been left in our hearts and within his role as a headteacher of Stretford Grammar school. Our Dad gave us fantastic memories growing up including a trip getting lost at night around Washington D.C but it was in his role as a Grandad where he truly excelled.

"At this time the family request privacy. Our love and memories of Michael will know no limits. We will love him forever, to Saturn and beyond."

View 3 Images Tributes have been left at the school gates of Stretford Grammar (Image: MEN Media)

Liz Bater, deputy headteacher at Stretford Grammar, confirmed the "sad and devastating news" in a letter to parents earlier this week.

She said: "I know that this news will be a dreadful shock to you and your children, and, as a community built up so strongly over so many years by our dear friend and colleague, Michael, we will all support each other during this awful period.

"As a staff body, we have worked with Michael for many years and the relationships created can never be replaced. However, in his honour and as a mark of his tireless hard work for Stretford Grammar School, we will pull together to continue his legacy."

Article continues below

Officers are continuing to appeal for information as they continue with their investigation. Witnesses, or anyone with relevant video footage from the area, are urged to contact 101 or use the online LiveChat function, quoting log number 2771 of April 20, 2026. Alternatively, call Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Octopus, British Gas, E.ON, EDF and OVO customers told 'your supplier must help'
News.content:
Octopus, British Gas, E.ON, EDF and OVO customers told 'your supplier must help'

Ofgem has issued an alert to gas and electricity customers who are worried about debt from high energy costs

View 2 Images Millions of people are in some form of energy debt (Image: Elaine Blackburne)

Energy bills have soared over recent years, along with many other essential household costs. The rise has often left people concerned over finding the money to get by or even with mounting debts.

‌



According to EDF Energy, the average monthly energy bill in the UK is £137 for a medium-sized household (2-3 people). This includes both gas and electricity. Costs vary depending on location, household size, and energy usage.

‌



This rises to £192 for a high usage household, typically four to five people. Smaller households of one or two people pay on average £99.

‌



But the bills have left millions struggling to pay. Energy UK says there are around two million households experiencing some form of energy debt, reaching a total of £5.5 billion.

View 2 Images Help is available from supply companies and government schemes (Image: Getty)

Ofgem has now issued an alert to tell people what they can do if they find themselves struggling to pay their bills. And it advises people they have "rights".

‌



In a post on X, formerly Twitter, it said: "If you’re in debt your supplier has to support you to get on top of your payments." In an accompanying video it said: "Are you struggling to pay for your energy? Energy debts - know your rights."

It continued: "Your supplier must treat you fairly. They must consider your circumstances such as ill health, pregnancy, low income, or other situations which mean you need support."

Ofgem said there were strict rules to be followed including on how people were billed. It advised: "Suppliers must use meter readings you provide to send clear and correct bills in a way you understand.

‌



"You can ask for bills in Braille, audio or another format that helps you understand. If you didn't get a bill, your energy supplier can't charge you for energy used over a year ago, unless you've made billing hard."

It also had advice on how to repay debts that have mounted up. It said: "If you're in debt, you may be able to agree a plan with your supplier to pay it back slowly, in a way you can afford.

"Your supplier must offer support that fits your needs, such as a better energy tariff, or directing you to independent free debt advice from organisations such as Citizens Advice."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The video went on to explain what to do if you are behind on repaying debt. It said: "If you're behind on repayments talk to your supplier. You might be able to take a break.

"You can change how you pay. Talk to your supplier to see if a prepayment meter works best for your situation.

Article continues below

"If you're eligible, your supplier will help you find the right support like hardship funds and schemes. Your supplier must try to help you,get in touch with them early. Their details are on your bill or online account."

In a separate post Ofgem advised energy users there are a number of different schemes available including benefits and grants from the government and suppliers. These include the Warm Home Discount Scheme, energy-saving improvement schemes and home energy support payments which are available to some people on benefits or a low income.

For full details of what is available visit here.

News.title: 'I took my dog to the zoo and couldn't believe what happened next'
News.content:
'I took my dog to the zoo and couldn't believe what happened next'

A woman who took her small dog to a zoo has shared the shocking interaction her pet had with one of the animals - as some say she made a mistake bringing her dog with her

View Image The dog owner soon realised taking her pup to the zoo was a mistake (stock photo) (Image: CazG Photography via Getty Images)

Zoos are fun experiences for the whole family, but it might be a good idea to leave your pets at home. Taking your children to the zoo for a day out can be a great experience, as not only do they get to see exotic animals up close, but they can also learn all about the importance of conservation and the efforts zoos make to save endangered species.

‌



But while zoos are great family days out, one woman on social media has demonstrated that it's probably not a good idea to bring your four-legged friends with you. Dog owner Jesenna Viila posted a video of her small dog, Liika, sitting outside an enclosure at a zoo, and captured the moment something astonishing happened.

‌



In the Instagram clip, a snow leopard inside the enclosure could be seen running up to the glass that separated it from Liika. It pawed at the glass and could be seen sniffing around as if it was trying to reach the dog - either to play with it or, potentially, do something more sinister to the tiny pup.

‌



Liika, however, was completely unfazed by the interaction. Not only did she barely flinch at the appearance of the big cat, but the dog even turned around and growled at the leopard as if she was annoyed at it being in her personal space.

Jesenna captioned the video: "Unfazed. Absolutely unfazed. She is scared of literally everything in the world, but a giant cat didn't make the cut. She even growled back: How dare you disturb my zen time."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The woman also uploaded a second video of the encounter from a different angle, which showed the snow leopard leaping over the rocks in its enclosure in order to try to reach Liika through the glass.

The second clip was captioned: "Zero survival instinct. She will steer away from random piles on the street, suspicious leftover snowballs, she is scared of literally everything, but she'll growl at a snow leopard like nobody's business."

However, many commenters were unimpressed by the videos. Many said that Jesenna was needlessly causing stress to both her dog and the snow leopard, when she could have left Liika at home or at least kept her away from the glass.

‌



One person said: "If you take your pet to the zoo, please do not leave them by the glass. This causes certain animals distress (which is exhibited by the snow leopard pawing at your pup). It may look like harmless fun, but it's creating a stressful environment for the animal in the habitat."

Another added: "Please don’t treat animals in captivity this way. It may be a source of amusement for you, but it isn't for the animals. Please."

A third wrote: "Why are you taking a dog to the zoo? Leave those animals alone. Their lives are hard enough."

‌



Can you take dogs to the zoo?

Taking dogs to the zoo in the UK depends entirely on which zoo or wildlife park you are visiting. Most major zoos in the UK are not dog-friendly, including Edinburgh Zoo, Chester Zoo, Whipsnade Zoo, and London Zoo. In all of these cases, only trained assistance dogs are permitted - and they must follow specific conditions that mean they can't enter walkthrough exhibits that put them in direct contact with other animals.

London Zoo's guidelines state: "At London Zoo, dogs and other animals are not permitted, except for certain assistance animals. The risk to London Zoo's animals and the assistance animals depends on the species, current health and security requirements, and history of the assistance animal; therefore, we do not encourage assistance animals other than dogs to enter our site."

There are some dog-friendly animal experiences in the UK, though, including Cotswold Wildlife Park and Gardens in Oxfordshire, Golders Hill Park Zoo in London, and Jimmy's Farm and Wildlife Park in Suffolk. In most of these cases, dogs must be kept on leads but are permitted to enter the park.

Article continues below

Always check with the zoo or wildlife park you intend on visiting before you bring your dog with you on your trip, as every location will have different rules and guidelines on bringing pets.

News.title: Dad who thought he had trapped wind almost died after fat jab mistake
News.content:
Dad who thought he had trapped wind almost died after fat jab mistake

Edd said all he could think about was leaving his children without a father

View 5 Images Edd thought his problem was trapped wind (Kennedy News and Media)

A dad who thought he had trapped wind after using weight loss jabs was told the pain was his gallbladder rotting - and it needed to be removed. Edd Langmead started his weight loss journey in May 2025 after struggling with his weight all his life, tipping the scales at 20st 7lbs at his heaviest.

‌



The 44-year-old, who suffered weight-related back pain, went to his GP and says he was told there was a waiting list of more than 12 months for weight-loss medication. Desperate for a 'quick fix', the musician decided to buy Mounjaro from an online pharmacy and says he saw 'instant' results.

‌



Due to a rise in costs, Edd tried a cheaper weight loss jab but says it wasn't as effective so switched back to Mounjaro. The dad-of-two says he didn't have any bad side effects and lost 5st 13lb in under a year, shrinking down to 14st 5lbs and eliminating his back pain.

‌



View 5 Images Edd in hospital being treated for his gallbladder illness (Kennedy News and Media)

But on March 9 this year, Edd started experiencing pain that he believed was trapped wind, and tried over-the-counter meds. Three days later Edd was left 'doubled over' in pain on the floor and his partner rang for an ambulance that blue-lighted him to hospital.

Doctors discovered he had gangrenous cholecystitis, a life-threatening condition where gallbladder tissue dies, and booked him in for surgery on March 13. The infection, which also spread into his stomach and lungs, is believed to be linked to his rapid weight loss.

‌



Lilly, which manufactures Mounjaro, said patient safety is their 'top priority'. Edd, from Oldham, said: "I've struggled with weight all my life. "I went to my doctor to get on it [weight loss injections] and they said that the waiting list is more than twelve months. Everyone wants a quick fix don't they? I did.

View 5 Images Edd in hospital (Kennedy News and Media)

"I'd been suffering with back pain for the past three years, getting out of bed actually hurt, and within the first two months my back pain had gone. I didn't have any bad side effects. It was up until that week, that's the first bit of pain [I had]. I've dealt with trapped wind quite a lot and I know what it feels like. I got all these things from over the counter trying to relieve it but it didn't do anything.

‌



"I couldn't sit or lie down without being in pain and it just kept getting worse and worse. My partner was meant to be going to work and I was doubled up in pain on the floor and could barely talk so she rang an ambulance."

After running tests, hospital staff rushed him into emergency surgery to have his gallbladder removed, where he stayed for four days before returning home with an IV antibiotic drip for 10 days. Edd said: "When I came out of the operation, a couple of the surgeons were saying how lucky I was.

View 5 Images Edd before his weight loss (Kennedy News and Media)

‌



"All I could think of was leaving my kids without a dad. I've gone from being the healthiest I've ever felt since I was a teenager to now, I feel like I'm in my nineties. I've got pipes hanging out of me, I can't walk or move properly, I can't lie down.

"If I had not gone in or if I had been in a different situation where I couldn't get to a hospital then I might not be here so that's the scary thing." After his experience, Edd quit the jabs and is now urging anyone wanting to use them to get them via their GP so they can be monitored.

Edd said: "Once I found out it'd all gone wrong and was related to weight loss it put doubt in me [and] that maybe I should've just waited for the NHS. The online companies don't show you those risks. There is a sadness that it happened like that for me because I'm sure that had I done it differently it wouldn't have been that way.

‌



"Make sure you go get regular blood tests. It's not worth the risk."

View 5 Images Edd after his weight loss (Kennedy News and Media)

A spokesman for Lilly, which manufactures Mounjaro, said: "Patient safety is Lilly’s top priority and we actively monitor, evaluate, and report safety information for all our medicines to the MHRA.

Article continues below

"The Mounjaro (tirzepatide) Patient Information Leaflet warns that cholecystitis (infection of the gallbladder) is an uncommon side effect (may affect up to 1 in 100 people). Anyone experiencing side effects when taking any Lilly medicine should consult their doctor or other healthcare professional, and should ensure that they are getting genuine Lilly medicine."

Acute cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder. It usually happens when a gallstone blocks the cystic duct. Without treatment, acute cholecystitis can sometimes lead to potentially life-threatening conditions including the death of gallbladder tissue (gangrenous cholecystitis), which can cause a serious infection that could spread throughout the body.

News.title: How Lineker and Neville became rival media moguls
News.content:
So what kind of challenge does Lineker and Neville's success pose to mainstream broadcasters?

"They are still niche, small businesses, admittedly with huge influence over fans and reach, but their turnover is very modest so they aren't taking on the big legacy media brands when it comes to hard business numbers", says Jimmy Worrall, who recently launched The Football Boardroom podcast after setting up a media business with former England manager Gareth Southgate.

"That said, they are taking eyeballs, and tapping into the shifting patterns of fans, and the way they consume sports news.

"Don't forget they don't have the real gold (premium live content).

"They are all trying to diversify and because they are nimble and entrepreneurial, and now have access to capital, they can now buy growth as well as take risk on new shows, both have speed to market and they could conceivably grow to be some significant media businesses if they invest heavily and quickly.

"They will need to constantly evolve, that is for sure." Worrall believes the pair's success can be explained because fans "have been under-served with information over the years...that's where long form podcasts have stepped in...combine it with a drastic lowering of financial and technology barriers, and new entrants surge in to meet this shifting demand."

He adds that The Rest is Football will be expected to perform a crucial function for Netflix during the World Cup, when the appetite for the streaming giant's content could drop off.

"It definitely makes life tricky for the established broadcaster," says Roger Mosey, a former BBC executive, when asked about the rise of athlete-driven content.

"The mainstream broadcasters are bound, overall, to be impartial - they can't be 'Manchester United TV' or 'the anti-VAR channel' or whatever.

"And they are still governed by regulation and their traditions, which means that they can't be as vigorous or sweary or impassioned as a podcast can."

During the 2024 Euros, Lineker faced scrutiny for being more outspoken about England's performances on his podcast than he was when presenting BBC coverage during the same tournament.

His 30-year relationship with the BBC then ended last year amid controversy over a social media post about Zionism.

In contrast, Neville continues to work for Sky as its leading pundit. Goldbridge has insisted he will continue to say what he wants since being acquired by The Overlap.

But is there a risk that an outburst about United could conflict with Neville's role at Sky, or his relationship with United or their fans?

"If I was Sky, I would be watching Stick to Football every week knowing there's no commercial upside but potential brand downside if the editorial tone is off brand because the talent is inextricably linked to Sky," says Worrall.

"If I was Neville I would be watching Mark Goldbridge thinking the same, except he has the commercial upside as well.

"It's one thing having a fan rant at the performance of the club, it's another to have one of the most decorated players in their history fund and facilitate that rant. That won't be an easy one to square off."

"We see it as being separate", insists Melvin. "There's no point investing in Mark and turning him into a traditional presenter. What we want to do is grow his channels with him."

Another factor was to have more of a daily offering via Goldbridge's channels.

"When [former United manager] Ruben Amorim was sacked we didn't have a Stick To Football show scheduled for 10 days so we didn't talk about it until then", recalls Melvin.

"We can't do that. We have to be able to be agile."

News.content:

Three days ago, People magazine posted a clip from an interview with actor Anne Hathaway, who is currently on a global press tour.

One of the questions concerned Hathaway’s feelings about ageing. In her response she – a non-Muslim – casually threw the word “inshallah” in mid-sentence.

The reaction was big.

The clip quickly went viral, with the incident reported on Al Jazeera, Grazia, and HuffPost, among others. Why has this moment struck such a chord with Muslims and Arabs worldwide?

So what does it mean?

Inshallah (also transliterated as “insha'Allah” and “inshaallah”) is an Arabic term that means “if God wills” or “God willing”.

open image in gallery The reaction to Anne Hathaway’s comment has been overwhelmingly positive ( PA )

The term is most commonly associated with Muslims, as the explicit exhortation to use “inshaallah” appears in the Quran, a revelation Muslims believe was first received by Muhammad in 610 CE.

Chapter 18, verses 23-24 instructs people not to say “I will do that in the future” without adding “inshaallah” – if God wills. Muslims regularly use the phrase in daily life as an affirmation that, ultimately, everything is under divine – not human – control.

The term is not exclusive to Muslims, however. Christian Arabs (particularly those that live among Muslims) will also regularly use it, as will other people from different communities (including non-religious people) living in Muslim countries.

‘Inshallah’ and pop culture

While the expression has a long history, and is meant to symbolise humanity’s submission to the divine will, its less lofty colloquial use is covered online.

Some Westerners who move to Muslim-majority countries have expressed their frustration at inshallah being used as a euphemism for “no”, when a person wants to avoid giving firm negative answer. Similarly, Muslim teens have made plenty of social media posts complaining about the relatable experience of their parents hiding behind “inshallah” when they really mean “no”. In this context, it’s more of a gentle letdown wrapped in divine decree.

open image in gallery Joe Biden used the term during a debate with Donald Trump ( AFP/Getty )

In recent years, we’ve seen several notable uses of the term by non-Muslims living in the West. Drake, for instance, used it in his 2018 song “Diplomatic Immunity”.

In 2020, Joe Biden invoked inshallah during his presidential debate with Donald Trump, when Trump was asked about his tax returns. Biden’s sarcastic tone implied he didn’t mean it in its literal sense.

The Muslim community’s response to Hathaway’s use of inshallah has been overwhelmingly positive, even if a small number are cynically viewing it as a publicity stunt targeting Arab and Muslim markets.

But most users are loving it, calling her “Anne Halal-away”, “Sister Anne-shallah Hathaway”, and “inshaAllah my princess of Genovia!!!”

It can be confusing to unfamiliar onlookers why some off-hand comments by celebrities can receive praise, and others vitriol.

Meme culture as a mode of belonging

So why has Hathway’s use of inshallah landed so well? To answer this, it helps to understand meme culture, as well as the shared experiences of modern, Western Muslims.

About the author Susan Carland is a Lecturer in the School of Social Sciences at Monash University. This article was originally published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

Take, for example, a highly memeified photo of a flyer stuck to a noticeboard advertising a “halal family movie night” for Finding Nemo 2.

At first glance, this photo (thought to originate in 2021) is unremarkable.

But it has the key ingredients to break from the confinement of its target audience (Muslim families wanting a movie night) and captivate broad sections of the internet, including non-Muslims. Namely, the endearingly amateur clip art design, the wholesome idea of a “halal movie night”, and the earnest and now iconic tagline, “inshallah they find him”.

“Inshallah they find him” has launched into many new memes, solidifying and ingratiating the phrase to countless online users over years.

Hathaway’s “inshallah” also came in a highly primed online environment.

Last week, the official Sesame Street social media accounts posted Elmo enthusiastically learning Arabic phrases from actor Ramy Youssef. Elmo learned “habibi” (“darling” or, as Elmo calls it, “special friend”) and “asalaamu ‘alaykum” (the Islamic greeting, “peace be upon you”), to the delight of many Muslims and Arabs.

These terms are important and beloved to many Arabs and Muslims. While only a minority of global Muslims are Arabs, Arabic as the language of the Quran is a lingua franca that binds Muslims through ritual practice.

When can non-Muslims use such terms?

Earlier this month, Trump posted an expletive-laden threat to the Iranian government concluding with the phrase, “Praise be to Allah”. The response to Trump’s post was intensely negative.

The responses to these different uses of Arab and Muslim expressions provides clarification for anyone wondering if, or when, it is ok for non-Muslims and non-Arabs to use these terms. Put simply, they are fine when used correctly, warmly, and without disrespect.

Trump’s use, conversely, was clearly designed to be belligerent and mocking. He took a phrase that is regularly used by Muslims, and which has profound religious significance, and turned it into a sarcastic insult pegged to a violent threat.

For Muslims and Arabs, who have felt their religion and cultures denigrated, pathologised, and held in contempt for hundreds of years by the West, Trump’s use was indefensible. And it is this same history that makes these communities particularly pleased when their expressions are acknowledged politely and affectionately.

No human likes their important expressions or practices being abused or mocked – but most do like to be affirmed. Hathaway got it right. Here’s to more of that, inshallah.

News.title: New Jersey college DNA team identifies 1979 murder victim as police work to identify his killer
News.content:

A New Jersey college DNA team has identified a murder victim in a cold case dating all the way to 1979. ​

The body was discovered in a shallow grave in a wooded area in Quinton Township, Salem County, 41 miles from Philadelphia. According to a statement from New Jersey State Police, the victim had suffered a gunshot wound to the head and died at some point during the winter of 1978-1979.

Now, the victim has been identified as Robert Dean Irelan by a team at the Ramapo College Investigative Genetic Genealogy Center.

The researchers told CBS News that they used DNA technology to search for family connections in the case. ​

open image in gallery The victim in a cold case dating all the way back to 1979 has been identified as Robert Dean Irelan ( New Jersey State Police )

“In this case, we knew that our John Doe was located in South Jersey,” Tracie Boyle, a case manager at Ramapo College, said. “So we had been looking for any kind of connections to the Atlantic City area, and we were able to find them pretty quickly.”

​Now, New Jersey State Police are searching for Irelan’s killer. The cops have already spoken to Irelan’s family, but are appealing to the public for more information.

​“We're really hoping that the public will reach out and have something that they can give to the law enforcement agency and help figure out who did this,” Boyle added.​

The victim was found wearing white painter’s trousers, a plaid cotton shirt and Pro-Keds sneakers. His distinctive blue jacket, which was made by Lee, featured a gold-plated letter “R” on its right pocket flap and a small gold-plated cross on the left pocket flap.​

Irelan’s body was also found clothed in a black-and-white pullover sweater. ​

According to police, he lived in Pleasantville, New Jersey, and was known for spending time in Atlantic City. ​

open image in gallery Irelan was found in a shallow grave wearing a distinctive Lee jacket, with a gold-plated 'R' on its front pocket ( New Jersey State Police )

The case was reopened in March 2023 and involved researchers carefully building a family tree in order to identify the victim.​

“We received a match list back from Match List Pro and Family Tree DNA, and we would just start building back the family trees of his genetic relatives, hoping to find common ancestors among them,” Boyle told WPVI.

​Before Irelan was identified, investigators released a composite sketch of the victim.

Eventually, a photograph of Irelan, whom investigators believe was in his late teens and early twenties, was found to match the victim.​

Herbert Ladner, a local resident who says he remembers hearing about the case when it first made headlines, told WPVI that the community is grateful for the advances in genetic technology.

​“I think it will keep the crime down a little bit and, if not, make a little easier on the people that’s got to process it,” he said.
